lesson.title: 1. How an order goes through the company
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Minh has just started as a sales assistant at an electronics company. On his first morning, his manager explains what happens to an order.*
lines: Before you start, let me quickly explain how an order goes through the company, **from start to finish**. It'll help you understand **who does what**.
That would be great. I was **a bit confused by** all the different teams yesterday.
Don't worry, everyone is at first. So, **it all starts with** us in sales. When a customer **places an order**, you **enter** it **into the system** and send them **a quote**.
Do I need to **get** the quote **approved**?
Only for big orders, anything over 50 million đồng. **In that case**, it **has to be signed off by** me first.

**Once** the customer has **paid the deposit**, the order goes to **finance**. They check the payment and **confirm** it in the system. You don't need to do anything **at that stage**, but **keep an eye on** it.
How long does that usually take?
Usually a day. If it's taking longer, just **give** finance **a quick call**. Don't just sit and wait.
Then it’s **passed on to** the warehouse. They pack everything and **book the delivery** with our **logistics team**. **As soon as** you get the delivery date, let the customer know.
So I'm the one who talks to the customer the whole time?
Exactly. You're their **main point of contact**. If there's a problem with the delivery, logistics will tell you, and you **keep the customer updated**.
That makes sense. Is there anything that often **goes wrong**?
Yes. Orders sometimes **get stuck** because finance hasn't confirmed the payment. So **my advice is to** check **the status of** your orders **first thing** every morning.
OK, **let me just check I've got this right**: sales, approval for big orders, finance, warehouse, then delivery. And I keep the customer updated.
Not right now, but I'm sure I'll have some later.
No problem. Just come and find me.

lesson.title: 2. Making Vietnamese coffee
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Tom is staying with his Vietnamese friend, Linh, for the weekend. In the morning, Linh makes cà phê phin and shows him how to do it.*
lines: Morning! Is that the coffee filter thing? I bought one last week, but **I've no idea how to** use it properly.
The *phin*? Yeah. What happened when you tried?
It **took forever**, and when it finally finished, it tasted like water.
That **happens to everyone at first**. Come here, I'll show you. **Start with** the condensed milk, about two spoons **in the bottom of** the glass.
Only two? I thought Vietnamese coffee was really sweet.
You can add more later if you like. **Then** put the *phin* **on top of** the glass and add the coffee, about two big spoons. **Give it a little shake** so it's flat.
OK. And this little metal thing goes on top?
Yeah, that's the press. Just put it on **gently**. **Don't push it down too hard, or** the water won't **get through**.
Ah, that's probably my mistake. I pressed it as hard as I could.
**That explains** why it took forever. **Now**, **pour in** just a little hot water, **enough to** cover the coffee, and wait about thirty seconds.
Why not **fill it up straight away**?
This bit **lets** the coffee **open up**. **Trust me**, it tastes much stronger. OK, now fill it **to the top**, put the lid on and **leave it to drip**.
Four or five minutes. **If** it's dripping really fast, the coffee isn't pressed enough. If it's **barely** dripping, it's too tight.
It's quite relaxing, actually, just watching it.
**That's half the fun. When it's done**, **give it a good stir** and pour it over ice.
Mmm. That's much better than mine.
See? Easy **once you know how**. You'll **get the hang of it**.

homework.title: Part 3: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to Sarah's guide for new employees, then complete the flow chart.

script.text: Hi everyone, and welcome to the company. I'm Sarah from the finance team. In this short guide, I'll walk you through how to claim your expenses after a business trip. It's pretty straightforward once you get the hang of it.

Step one: During your trip, ==keep all your receipts==: for taxis, meals, hotels, everything. For hotels, make sure you ask for ==a proper invoice== with the company's name on it, or we won't be able to accept it.
Step two: Once you're back in the office, log in to the HR app and ==fill in the expenses form==. ==Take a clear photo of each receipt== and upload it to the form.

Step three: When you submit the form, it goes straight to your manager, who needs to ==approve== it before we can do anything. If your claim is over five million đồng, it also has to be signed off by ==the head of the department==. If it's under five million, it comes straight to us.
Step four: After that, the claim is passed on to us in ==the finance team==. We check everything carefully, so please double-check your numbers before you submit.
Step five: As soon as everything is confirmed, the money is paid into ==your bank account==, usually within ==ten working days==.
And finally, one important tip: please submit your claim before ==the end of the month==. That's where most people go wrong. Late claims get stuck in the system and can take much longer.
If you have any questions, you can always give us a quick call or drop us an email. Thanks, and good luck in your new role!
